D14 measured the shared economic exit screen at recall 2/6 with a gas-concentration bias on the NEISO crossover window (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d14-neiso-t1x-2026-08-30.md §2); the same screen composes every bundle's exits, so every model-side fleet-composition value here carries that measured skill caveat (golden finding §4(ii)).

AEO2025 reference froze law as of Dec 2024 (pre-OBBBA, CAA §111 in force), so its coal exit path is regulatory-assumption-heavy and its offshore-wind pipeline predates the 2025 federal cancellations — a source-vintage caveat cutting both directions (corridor memo D4 precedent).

The committed summaries carry NO generation-by-fuel, so the 252 AEO energy-mix (generation) anchors are NOT dispositioned — they remain context; extending the trajectory reporting grain is routed to the director (a reporting gap, not a divergence).

The trajectory's capacity_by_fuel_mw excludes LP storage resources (batteries and pumped storage) — run_full_horizon._capacity_by_fuel iterates generator fuels only — so the storage rows below quote the model's storage fleet from its registry base (STORAGE_BASE_FLEET_MW, EIA-860 2025 ER, src/market_sim/config/capacity_market.py:487) plus the window's builds_storage_mw ledger (zero in every bundle). AEO pumped-storage anchors are left as context (both sides hold PS roughly flat).

rows.explanation: −14.1 % — inside the corridor, at its edge; the deficit is the solar/storage/CT rows' explained gaps net of retained coal.

Ours: 41.16 GW retained — the S-123-V verification measured the window's exit list as 2027 gas_st 389.5 MW, 2029 oil 3,295.8 MW, 2030 nuclear 617.0 + biomass 16.0 MW — NO economic coal exit; the −1.6 GW coal delta vs the 2026 base is the confirmed exit/derate registry (the FFR-1A recorder). Under retirement_rule='pipeline' the economic screen retires coal only when the attainable inframarginal margin (energy+AS+capacity legs, spec §5.2) falls below FOM-only going-forward cost, and at these solved margins it does not; the confirmed-exit registry (spec §5.1 step 0 — the ONLY exogenous fossil exit channel) removes just the instrument-bound units. Theirs: AEO2025 reference retires to 18.6 GW by the anchor year, driven by CAA §111 compliance dates frozen into its Dec-2024 law baseline — a regulation the model deliberately does not hard-code (corridor memo D4/D8 precedent: a policy-input choice, not a screen success — and D14's measured exit-recall caveat applies to any claim of retirement skill). Composition note (not the verdict): 8.99 GW of the model's 36.33 GW combined-cycle fleet is CCS-retrofitted by this year — the spec §5.6 retrofit screen converting at its 3 GW/yr/ISO cap from ccs_retrofit_available_year=2028 (ira_ccus_45q_last_year=2032); the resolved carbon signal is zero for this ISO (no armed state carbon program — PJM's partial-footprint RGGI registry is gated off by default, MISO has none), so the 45Q window alone carries the retrofit economics. AEO2025's regional CC rows carry no comparable CCS conversion. The capacity aggregate matches; the emissions consequence is dispositioned on the co2 row. D21 measured this screen's paired-arm behavior; D23 attributed the P1 FAIL to the arm construction (a nonzero carbon_price override REPLACES the resolved signal, so the $25 arm CUT it) — the screen's carbon-price response is sign-correct (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d23-p1-carbon-sign-2026-09-01.md).

Ours: 37.46 GW — S-123-V measured ZERO economic entry and zero backstop build in the whole window (additions 769.8 MW, all EIA-860 planned; the corrected requirement removed the backstop's trigger), and the 2029 economic oil exit (−3.3 GW) removes steam capacity AEO's Fossil Steam column retains. Theirs: AEO builds Midcontinent CT 44.5→71.4→85.1 GW across 2030→2040 (committed anchor slope, ~+2.7 GW/yr) — the corridor memo D3 national gas revival at its largest regional expression. A residual base-fleet offset (model CT+steam base 41.1 GW in 2026 vs AEO's higher implied baseline) is the EMM-footprint/classing approximation each anchor row's note carries. Three legs, all named; the dominant one is AEO's build program vs the model's measured zero-entry window.
−11.6 %: inside the corridor (the model's 617 MW 2030 nuclear exit is a confirmed-registry instrument; AEO holds the fleet).

Ours: 7.0 GW, FLAT across the window — the committed-status EIA-860 pipeline delivers +4.0 GW wind and ZERO solar for MISO, and S-123-V measured economic entry at 0 MW in every year (its §6 step 3) even with entry_vre_capacity_revenue=True in this bundle — so the gap is the entry screen's solar economics, not a missing revenue leg. The MISO RPS-analogue constraint sits at its $30 ACP ceiling all window (committed rps_dual), pressing for clean energy the entry machinery does not deliver as PV. This is the corridor's known zero-solar-entry family (BLK-8 was the ERCOT measurement; the MISO evidence here is this bundle's own measured window) — a registered root-cause object, largest single-tech divergence in this table.

Ours: 1.85 GW — the EIA-860/eGRID grid-registry biomass+waste fleet, which includes IPP/CHP wood and municipal-waste units that serve the grid. Theirs: AEO's 'Electric Power Sector' capacity excludes end-use/CHP-sector capacity, so its wood+MSW rows (0.83 GW summed) sit structurally below a grid-registry count.
